a-loaf-of.exampleUsage: They bought a loaf of bread.

a-dozen.definition: A quantity made up of exactly twelve items.

a-slice-of.definition: One thin, flat piece cut from a larger food item.
a-slice-of.exampleUsage: She asked for a slice of cheese.

a-piece-of.definition: One separate portion or part of something.
a-piece-of.exampleUsage: He chose a piece of fruit.

a-pack-of.definition: A group of items sold together in one package.
a-pack-of.exampleUsage: They bought a pack of paper towels.

a-handful-of.definition: An amount small enough to fit in one hand, used as an approximate quantity.
a-handful-of.exampleUsage: She added a handful of grapes to the bowl.

a-pint-of.definition: A quantity with a volume of one pint; the exact size depends on the measurement system used.
a-pint-of.exampleUsage: The recipe used a pint of cream.

a-stick-of.definition: One long narrow unit of a product sold in stick form, such as butter or gum.
a-stick-of.exampleUsage: The recipe called for a stick of butter.

organic.definition: Of or relating to foodstuff grown or raised without synthetic fertilizers or pesticides or hormones.

gluten-free.definition: Made without gluten-containing ingredients, according to applicable food-labeling standards.

sugar-free.definition: Containing no sugar or an amount low enough to meet the relevant food-labeling definition.

low-fat.definition: Containing a relatively small amount of fat and meeting any applicable labeling standard.

frozen.definition: Kept at a temperature low enough to turn water into ice.

on-sale.definition: Being offered for purchase at a reduced price or under a special promotion.
on-sale.exampleUsage: The cereal is on sale this week.

buy-1-get-1-free.definition: A sales promotion in which buying one eligible item includes a second eligible item at no additional price under the stated terms.
buy-1-get-1-free.exampleUsage: The sign advertised a buy-one-get-one-free promotion.
buy-1-get-1-free.arabicTranslation: اشترِ واحدًا واحصل على الثاني مجانًا

best-before.definition: A date indicating the period during which a food is expected to retain its best quality; it is not always the same as a safety expiration date.
best-before.exampleUsage: The package shows a best-before date.

nutrition-facts.definition: Standardized label information showing a food's energy and nutrient amounts per stated serving or quantity.
nutrition-facts.exampleUsage: The shopper read the nutrition-facts panel.

non-gmo.definition: A label indicating that a product meets a specified standard regarding the use of genetically modified organisms.
non-gmo.exampleUsage: The package carries a non-GMO label.

vegan.exampleUsage: The vegan was identified during the lesson.

how-much-is-this-.definition: A question used to ask the price of an item.
how-much-is-this-.exampleUsage: A shopper asked, 'How much is this?'

where-can-i-find-.definition: A question used to ask where a particular item or section is located.
where-can-i-find-.exampleUsage: She asked, 'Where can I find rice?'

paper-or-plastic-.definition: A checkout question asking which type of shopping bag a customer prefers.

is-this-on-sale-.definition: A question used to ask whether an item has a reduced promotional price.
is-this-on-sale-.exampleUsage: The shopper asked, 'Is this on sale?'

cash-or-card-.definition: A checkout question asking whether payment will be made with cash or a payment card.

do-you-have-.definition: A question used to ask whether a store has a particular item available.
do-you-have-.exampleUsage: The customer asked, 'Do you have oat milk?'

can-i-get-a-bag-.definition: A polite question used to request a shopping bag.
can-i-get-a-bag-.exampleUsage: She asked, 'Can I get a bag?'

i-need-a-refund.definition: A statement used to say that you want money returned for a purchase, subject to the store's return policy.
i-need-a-refund.exampleUsage: The customer said, 'I need a refund,' and showed the receipt.

where-is-aisle-.definition: A question used to ask the location of a numbered or named store aisle.

is-this-fresh-.definition: A question used to ask whether food is recently prepared, harvested, or still in good condition.

can-i-taste-this-.definition: A polite question asking whether a store permits a sample of a food item.
can-i-taste-this-.exampleUsage: The customer asked staff, 'Can I taste this?'

i-have-a-coupon.definition: A statement used to tell a cashier that you have a coupon or discount voucher for the purchase.
i-have-a-coupon.exampleUsage: The shopper said, 'I have a coupon,' before payment.

ginger.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Ginger" in an educational description.
ginger.definition: A spicy root used to flavor food and drinks.

cart.definition: Wheeled vehicle that can be pushed by a person.

salami.definition: Highly seasoned fatty sausage of pork and beef usually dried.

hummus.definition: A thick spread made from mashed chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice and garlic.
